newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel firm, low sulphur steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel firm, low sulphur steady.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil prices were firmer on Tuesday amid continuing good demand in Europe for bunker fuel and signs of some interest from utilities for end-month cargoes, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $117, $117.50 and $118 in the morning and then moved up to $119 in the afternoon.

Cargoes were steady to firmer. One utility player said offers had not moved far above $118 cif NWE, with at least one offer seen out of ARA. A Scandinavian player sold a mid January cargo on Friday but details of the sale were confidential.
Low sulphur markets were weighed down by good supply and by a lack of indications that Italians would buy product for January.
At least four cargoes were thought to be available out of northwest Europe and offers into Italy for late January were heard at, or slightly below, $130 cif Milazzo.
Offers were also seen for late January/early February from the U.S., although offer prices were not discussed.
